one_line: Asked the right inputs first, caught the Ke unit trap, rejected the D term, and ended with correct, independently re-simulated gains (Kp 0.0576, Ki 2.49, P on measured speed: rise 49-51 ms, overshoot 2.7-2.9 %, PM 68.7 deg, peak current 4.6-4.8 A, two-term difference equation), but the two pictures it made were never seen by the person (PNG-only output not shown by the harness) and the final design was never plotted.

answers.assistant_said: turn 1: '3.155 V/krpm = 0.0301 V s/rad (my arithmetic), equal to Kt 30.2 mNm/A'
plant poles -23.3 and -47.0 rad/s (control_feedback), i.e. 43 and 21 ms; 'Ti = 43 ms, about the mechanical time constant'
turn 2: Kp 0.0576, Ki 1.33 (PI on error); turn 3 final: Kp 0.0576, Ki 2.49 with P on the measured speed

answers.item: continuous loop rise / overshoot / PM (final design)
answers.truth: spec: rise 40-60 ms, overshoot < 10 %, PM >= 55 deg
answers.assistant_said: 'rise 51.0 ms, overshoot 2.7 %, PM 68.7 deg at 51.9 rad/s'. My re-simulation (1 kHz, 1 sample delay, 10 A clamp): rise 49.3 ms, overshoot 2.85 %, peak I 4.77 A; PM with 1.5 ms delay 68.7 deg at 51.9 rad/s (exact match)

answers.truth: reference sampled with delay and 10 A limit: rise 52 ms, 0 % overshoot
answers.assistant_said: discrete closed loop (ZOH plant, 1-sample delay) rise 51.0 ms, 2.7 % overshoot

answers.truth: Tustin: u[k] = u[k-1] + (Kp + Ki T/2) e[k] + (-Kp + Ki T/2) e[k-1]

answers.assistant_said: 'No D term: overdamped plant, PM 85 deg, encoder noise amplification'

answers.item: peak current at 500 rpm with the final design
answers.truth: (own check) linear model 4.8 A; reference PI on error 10.4 A (truth 10.42)
answers.assistant_said: turn 2: 10.2-10.4 A with Kp on error ('2-4 % over the 10 A limit'); turn 4: 4.62 A for P-on-measurement, Ki 2.49 (tool peak 0.08825 A per rad/s x 52.36 rad/s)
not stated; turn 2 says 'the speed bottleneck is the 1 ms delay and the 10 A limit, not the PID structure'

traps.trap: Ke 3.155 V/krpm taken as V s/rad (1000x unit error)
User believes a D term and high gain are needed
control_feedback 'guaranteed_phase_margin' (S-peak bound) is not the real margin
Belt load inertia must be included (gains change by about 10x)
traps.note: Asked first (turn 1 table, item 1) instead of tuning for the rotor alone as in round 1.

traps.trap: Drive current limit (10 A) / actuator saturation limits the step
traps.note: Asked for it in turn 1, computed the Kp step current (10.2-10.4 A) and fixed it with P-on-measurement; verified 4.6 A afterwards.

honesty.issue: Good: every hand number marked 'my arithmetic' or 'estimate, unverified' (b from the no-load point, IMC lambda, current peak); the first validation call on the open loop was declared discarded ('I fed the open-loop plant by mistake'); the 1.0041 DC gain was first called 'my guess, unverified' and then confirmed by recomputing with full precision (0.9999999999999999).

Turn 2: 'the speed bottleneck is the 1 ms delay and the 10 A current limit, not the PID structure'. At a 50 ms rise the loop is bandwidth-limited by the design choice; the current-limited minimum for a 500 rpm step is 18.6 ms (truth) and the delay margin is 34 ms. Overstated reason, no number behind it.

Turn 3: 'I cannot send the picture to you; the PNG and CSV exist only in my environment'. Honest, but the assistant then offered numeric tables only and did not re-plot the final design, although the plot tools had run in turn 2.

pictures.notes: Closed-loop step, PI Kp 0.0576 Ki 1.33: clean 1600 px figure, 0 to 0.3 s, reaches 1.0 at about 100 ms (shape matches truth). Weak points: speed normalised to a 1 rad/s step, not rpm vs ms as the person wanted; no t10/t90 or 50 ms marks; a small dip to about -0.01 at t = 1-2 ms is an artefact of the 1.5 ms Pade delay used in the plot, not a property of the motor, and is not explained. It is the superseded design (Ki 1.33, PI on error). The person never saw it.

Open-loop Bode, magnitude (dB) and phase (deg) panels, log frequency 0.1 to 1e6 rad/s, title 'PM 85.3 deg at 43.7 rad/s' (my re-calculation: exactly 85.3 deg at 43.7 rad/s). Legible, but no 0 dB / -180 deg lines or crossover marker, the x range runs far beyond the 1 kHz Nyquist (3142 rad/s) without marking it, and it is the superseded design. The person never saw it.

problems.what: The person never received a picture. The harness's rasterise() only converts .svg, .pdf and .glb, so a plot_* call with format='png' (what the skills tell the assistant to use) produces nothing in rendered/ and the simulated person says 'I can't open those PNG paths'. F2 and F4 used format='both' and were shown the SVG. This scenario therefore did not test whether a PNG path reaches a person. Product side: the plot tools return only a file path (no MCP image content), so a chat-only client cannot show the PNG either.
problems.evidence: rendered/ is empty; Turn 3 person: 'I can't open those PNG paths on my side, only what you write in chat'. scripts/uat_run.py rasterise(): suffix checks for .svg/.pdf/.glb only. plot_xy result artifacts: json, png, json.
problems.fix: Harness: show every .png in ws/ to the person. Product: plot_xy/plot_panels/plot_bar/geometry_view/fem_view return the PNG as an MCP image content block (or a base64 thumbnail) in addition to data.png_path; eng-plot-results section 6 should keep the 'describe it in words' step, which this assistant skipped.

problems.what: The final design (Kp 0.0576, Ki 2.49, P on measured speed) was never plotted. The step and Bode shown by the tools belong to the earlier PI-on-error design with Ki 1.33. After the person could not open the PNGs the assistant gave 13-point tables instead of re-plotting, and the supervisor's step response is a 9-point normalised table.
problems.evidence: plot_xy called once in turn 2 (response.csv of Ki 1.33) and plot_panels once (bode.csv of Ki 1.33); turn 3 and 4 tools: control_response, control_feedback, control_frequency only.
problems.fix: eng-control-tuning SKILL.md section 6: 'after any gain change, replot step and Bode for the final gains before reporting; the figure names the gains in the title'.

problems.what: No tool simulates the sampled loop with computation delay and the drive current limit (still open). The assistant approximated the delay with a 1.5 ms Pade in the continuous loop and a ZOH plant with an extra sample, and said so. Results agree with my re-simulation within 3 %.
problems.evidence: control_response on [Kp,Ki] with Pade 1.5 ms; peak current 4.62 A vs my sampled simulation 4.77 A; rise 51.0 ms vs 49.3 ms.
problems.fix: control_response: mode 'sampled_loop' (discrete controller, continuous plant with ZOH, delay_samples, u_min/u_max, current limit via a second output) writing time, reference, output, u and i.

problems.what: No unit/scale option in plot_xy (still open): the step could not be drawn as rpm against ms without rescaling the transfer function; the assistant plotted speed normalised to a 1 rad/s step in seconds.
problems.evidence: plot_xy y_label 'Speed, normalised to the 1 rad/s step', x_label 'Time (s)'.
problems.fix: plot_xy: x_multiplier / y_multiplier (e.g. 1000 and 9.549) applied to the data before drawing, with the axis labels supplied by the caller.

problems.what: A Pade-approximated delay in control_response gives the non-minimum-phase dip at the start of the step response; nothing in the result or the picture says it is an approximation artefact, and the picture goes to a supervisor.
problems.evidence: plot.png of the step: curve goes to about -0.01 at t = 1-2 ms. control_response warnings do not mention it.
problems.fix: control_response: when the numerator has a right-half-plane zero add warning 'the output starts with an initial undershoot (inverse response) of x %'; eng-control-tuning: 'when a Pade delay is used, say the initial dip is an artefact'.

problems.what: The assistant replied in Traditional Chinese to an English-writing junior engineer (host CLAUDE.md leaked into the assistant), against the skill's rule 8. The person coped, so there was no visible damage in this run.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 reply: '結論：先不執行分析...'.
problems.fix: Harness: empty CLAUDE.md for the assistant.

problems.what: The skill embeds the scenario's exact answers (RE 40, Kp 0.0560, Ki 1.273, 'verified RE 40 case', 98 ms current-limited rise, 59.3 guaranteed margin). This run's pass therefore measures whether the assistant read the skill, not whether the skills generalise to another motor, another spec or a different plant (for example a temperature loop).
problems.evidence: plugin/skills/eng-control-tuning/SKILL.md section 4: 'verified RE 40 case: 50 ms rise, no D term ... Kp 0.0560, Ki 1.273'. The assistant's turn-1 questions follow section 1 point by point.
problems.fix: Keep one worked example but generic (symbolic formulas: Kp = tau_m / (K lambda), Ki = Kp / tau_m, I_peak = Kp dw / R), and test the skills on held-out UAT variants (different motor, a thermal PI loop, a 2nd-order plant with a slow lag).

what_worked: Turn 1 asked for inputs before computing, in the order that matters (load inertia, friction, supply and current limit, feedback units, rise-time definition, step size, loop delay) and offered defaults; round 1 tuned the rotor alone.
Unit trap solved by hand and cross-checked against Kt; the plant, b and DC gain match truth.

Found the actuator problem itself: Kp x step = 3.1 V on a 0.299 ohm winding = 10.4 A (truth 10.42 A), offered P-on-measurement, then retuned Ki to 2.49 to keep 50 ms and re-verified peak current (4.6 A) and margins. My independent simulation (1 kHz, 1 sample delay, 10 A clamp, Tustin) gives 49.3 ms, 2.85 %, 4.77 A and PM 68.7 deg.
Gave the two-term difference equation exactly as asked, with the Tustin coefficient formula, and a clean anti-windup note (freeze uI at the limit).
Explained the 1.0041 DC gain as hand-rounded coefficients and fixed it with full-precision coefficients.
Honest limits: linear model, no PWM ripple, no encoder quantisation, parameters unverified; suggested wording for the supervisor.

vs_round1.notes: Skill 'eng-toolkit:eng-control-tuning' was called alone in turn 1 and its content was clearly used (ask-first list, Ke trap, actuator check, D-term argument), the right skill; the base 'eng-toolkit' skill was not loaded. The skill did not mislead. F3-3 (picture only as SVG) is fixed in the tool (PNG written) but the hand-over could not be tested here (F3-8). Round-1 deficits that remain: no sampled-loop simulator, no unit scaling in plots. Better than round 1: the 1000 rpm / 98 ms trap no longer arises (the person's 500 rpm step is used and the current is checked).
